Le masse renali si dividono in espansive:
Renal masses are divided into expansile and infiltrative. Clear cell carcinoma grows in an expansile manner: it deforms the contour, has sharp margins and is hypervascular. Urothelial carcinoma of the pelvis instead infiltrates from the sinus toward the parenchyma, preserves the "bean-shaped" form of the kidney, is hypovascular, and on the excretory phase causes filling defects or non-opacified calyces ("phantom calyx", amputation).
Other infiltrative lesions: lymphoma, metastases, collecting duct carcinoma, pyelonephritis (different clinical context).
The diagnosis matters for treatment: for upper tract urothelial carcinoma, nephroureterectomy with bladder cuff excision is performed (not partial nephrectomy), and the bladder is monitored (synchronous or metachronous tumors are frequent). The right exam for hematuria is CT urography with excretory phase.
